title: Auto Dealership License Database
demand_signal: Exceptionally strong and validated. 10+ commercial vendors actively selling auto dealership email lists: LeadsPlease (108,548 contacts), BookYourData (167,607 contacts), BlueMailMedia (300K+ emails, updated April 2026), InfoGlobalData (51,932 records), AverickMedia (57,374 emails). CampaignLake published a '7 Best Auto Dealers Email List Providers for 2026' roundup — vendor ecosystem maturity is unmistakable. Data decay rate of 25-30% annually means buyers must repurchase regularly.
target_audience: Auto dealership CRM/DMS software vendors (CDK Global, DealerSocket, VinSolutions, Tekion, AutoRaptor) running outbound sales campaigns; automotive parts and equipment distributors targeting dealership service departments; F&I product providers (warranty companies, GAP insurance); digital marketing agencies specializing in dealership SEO/SEM; dealership consulting firms; auto auction companies (Manheim, ADESA) recruiting dealer buyers; automotive lenders and floor plan financing companies
public_data_sources: California DMV Occupational License Lookup (OLSIS) — searchable, no auth required
Texas DMV Motor Vehicle Dealer List (texasdmv.my.salesforce-sites.com/dealers)
DC DMV Active Dealers List — published as downloadable document, updated monthly
South Carolina DMV — View Dealer License Information portal
Data.gov catalog — listing of licensed automobile dealers (nightly updates, some states)
State Secretary of State business registries (all 50 states)
competitive_landscape: Crowded at the premium tier: BookYourData, LeadsPlease, InfoGlobalData, BlueMailMedia, AverickMedia, eSalesData, ContactLists.com all sell dealer lists at subscription or per-contact pricing ($0.10-$0.50/contact). No vendor offers a clean, one-time downloadable state-by-state CSV at a flat price. DataStructured wedge: $49-$79 per state CSV vs. $200-$500+ subscription commitments. Public DMV licensing data is free but fragmented across 50 states with inconsistent formats — cleaning and standardizing is the value-add.
monetization_model: One-time state-specific CSVs at $49-$79 each. Bundle: 'Top 10 States Auto Dealer Database' at $199 (vs. $500+ from competitors). Fields: dealership name, DBA, license type (new/used/wholesale), license number, owner/principal name, address, phone, license status, issue/expiration dates. Revenue path: 50 state SKUs × steady demand from CRM/DMS sales teams.
estimated_market_size: ~50,000 franchised dealerships + ~60,000 independent used car dealers in the US. Buyer LTV: CRM/DMS software costs $99-$3,000/month per rooftop ($1,200-$36,000/year), meaning a single closed deal from a $49 lead list generates 24x-734x ROI for the buyer. Auto dealership CRM market valued at $2.5B+ in 2026.
data_freshness_requirement: Quarterly updates recommended. License renewal cycles vary by state (annual or biennial). Data decay at 25-30% annually due to ownership changes, closures, and new entrants.
compliance_notes: PASS potential: All data sourced from state DMV occupational licensing records — public information by law. No PII beyond business owner names (already public record). Dealer license status is consumer protection information. Source attribution via state DMV portal URLs.
next_steps: Harvest Texas DMV dealer list (large market, Salesforce-hosted portal, likely API-friendly)
Harvest California OLSIS dealer records (largest state market)
Clean and standardize into unified schema across states
Launch TX + CA as first two SKUs on Gumroad at $49 each
Target r/AutoDealership, LinkedIn auto industry groups for distribution
researcher_notes: One of the strongest signals this scan. The 10+ vendor ecosystem with transparent pricing (CampaignLake literally published a '7 Best' roundup) is textbook demand validation. The key differentiator is format + price: nobody sells a clean one-time state CSV at $49. Everyone forces you into subscriptions or per-contact pricing. Public DMV data is freely available but scattered across 50 different state portals in different formats — the cleaning and standardization IS the product. Start with TX and CA (largest dealer populations), then expand state-by-state. High buyer LTV from CRM/DMS vendors makes even a $49 price point extremely attractive to purchasers.
